note: Independent style interpretations. Brand names identify inspiration, not affiliation or product recommendations.

codes.label: Rio meets the countryside
codes.statement: A loud colour or print against an easy, lived-in shape. Try a vivid dress with practical shoes, or clash two colours you already love.
codes.accessory: Finish with your brightest scarf, woven bag, or a bold earring.
codes.route: Start with one expressive piece you already own. Change the accessory; if a gap remains, consider a well-made secondhand piece.

codes.label: Romantic volume, sharp colour
codes.statement: Let a dress or soft blouse carry the shape, then ground it with a strong second colour and an everyday shoe.
codes.accessory: Add a defined belt, sculptural earring, or a small bag with presence.
codes.route: Restyle a dress with a belt or layer. Inspect seams, fabric and care before adding another piece.

codes.label: The shoe is the statement
codes.statement: Build a simple colour story, then let an embellished or contrasting shoe be the point of view.
codes.accessory: Echo the shoe with one earring, scarf, or bag detail; keep the rest useful and wearable.
codes.route: Let the most expressive shoes you own lead. For another pair, consider repairability and the wears you can realistically give it.

codes.label: Colour on colour
codes.statement: Mix two saturated shades instead of treating one as the accent. A strong top and trouser pairing can do all the talking.
codes.accessory: Repeat one of the colours in a scarf or bag, or add a third small pop.
codes.route: Recombine two saturated colours already in your closet. An enduring accessory can give the pairing a new direction.
